headline_seed: Appeals court rejects Rep. McIver's challenge to charges for alleged assaults at ICE facility - Politico

consensus_facts: All three outlets' headlines agree that a federal appeals court rejected Rep. LaMonica McIver's challenge and allowed the criminal case tied to the Delaney Hall ICE facility clash to proceed.
All three outlets reference the panel being split, with The Hill and Politico specifically framing the split around selective/retaliatory prosecution claims.

framing_analysis.Politico: Only outlet with retrievable full body text. Politico reports the 3rd Circuit ruled 2-1 that Rep. LaMonica McIver is not immune from prosecution for contact with ICE officials during a May 2025 oversight visit to New Jersey's Delaney Hall detention facility. Reports she faces three federal charges related to alleged assaults on and interference with ICE officials. Names the majority as Judge Cindy Chung (Biden appointee) and Judge Stephanos Bibas (Trump appointee), who rejected the 'speech or debate' clause immunity argument for two of three charges because the altercation occurred outside the facility. Reports the majority sent the third charge back to the trial judge for closer review because the indictment doesn't specify officer locations or precise conduct. Emphasizes the partial dissent of Judge Thomas Ambro (Clinton appointee), who argued McIver should be able to pursue evidence the prosecution was retaliatory, quoting him on the constitutional risks of retaliatory prosecutions and noting his comparison to the dismissed Jan. 6 assault charges. Provides political context: charges originally brought by former Trump lawyer and White House aide Alina Habba; McIver claims political motivation.
framing_analysis.The Washington Post: Headline-only (no retrievable body text). Frames the story around the case being allowed to 'proceed,' referencing the 'Delaney Hall clash' and the appeals court ruling. Neutral, event-focused headline language.
framing_analysis.The Hill: Headline-only (no retrievable body text). Frames the story as the court 'declines to toss' the case and emphasizes the panel 'splits on selective prosecution claims,' foregrounding the dissent/selective-prosecution angle in its headline.

primary_source_alignment: No primary source (the 3rd Circuit opinion) was located in the dossier. Politico quotes directly from the opinion (Judge Chung's 'unambiguously non-legislative' language and Judge Ambro's dissent), but these excerpts could not be independently verified against the underlying document.
missing_context: Only one of three articles (Politico) has retrievable full body text. The Washington Post and The Hill entries are headline-only and cannot corroborate Politico's body-level details, so specific facts (charge count, judges' names, vote breakdown, dissent reasoning) are single-source and not true consensus.
No primary source — the actual 3rd Circuit opinion — was included in the dossier, so all quoted judicial language rests on Politico's rendering alone.
None of the retrievable coverage details what penalties McIver faces if convicted, the current status/schedule of the underlying trial, or McIver's own response to the ruling.
No article explains the procedural avenue for 'further appeals' that Politico's subhead references (e.g., en banc review or Supreme Court petition), beyond noting the 2-1 split may leave one open.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Only one outlet (Politico) provided full body text while the other two are headline-only, so there is insufficient multi-outlet body-level divergence to justify META; the responsible move is a straightforward REPORT attributing the substantive details to Politico and noting the single-source limitation.

articles.title: Case against lawmaker charged in Delaney Hall clash can proceed, appeals court rules - The Washington Post
Appeals court declines to toss McIver case as panel splits on selective prosecution claims - The Hill
